title: GET /api/iam/login-config?client=<azp>
description: Everything the frontend needs to start a standard OIDC authorization-code + PKCE login, and nothing vendor-specific. The frontend fetches discovery_url and takes authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, jwks_uri and end_session_endpoint from it (LOGIN.md). Public, through the edge.

client.description: The platform client this configuration is for (the azp of the tokens it will receive).

issuer.description: The IdP's issuer as the browser sees it; the frontend checks that discovery's issuer equals it.

discovery_url.description: issuer + /.well-known/openid-configuration, as the browser reaches it.

client_id.description: The IdP client id registered for this platform client: a public client, no secret.

scopes.description: Always contains openid; never offline_access (the platform session is the member's refresh token, not the IdP's).

end_session_supported.description: Whether discovery has an end_session_endpoint the frontend may call with id_token_hint and post_logout_redirect_uri.

extra_authorize_params.description: Member-specific query parameters added to the authorization request (for example a Keycloak kc_idp_hint). Values are strings; the frontend adds them without interpreting them.
